text:
Anya: small design sync  experimenting with tapered TTL leases + decay scoring for dedicated pool soft allocation. want to avoid hard reservations but give better steady-state guarantees.
Micah: "tapered TTL" = variable lease lengths based on recent usage?
Anya: yes. short bursts get short TTLs (302s), steady flows get longer but still non-binding leases (up to 5m). each lease has a decay score used by placement.
James: how do we compute decay score?
Anya: sketch: score = alpha * recent_qps + beta * renew_count - gamma * time_since_last_renew. normalized per-tenant. scheduler prefers higher scores when placing on hot pools.
Lia: sounds reasonable. what about churn - noisy tenants renewing every 10s?
Micah: add exponential backoff multiplier on renewals and a renewal_quota window. after X renewals in Y seconds, mark tenant as "churny" and lower score.
James: do we still need warmup tokens?
Anya: yes, but make them part of score rather than separate resource. token grants + small warm-cache allocation (not full GPU) for a brief window (10s).
Lia: operator architecture: should contract bookkeeping live inside the main operator or a sidecar contract-manager?
Micah: I'd prefer sidecar. keep lease generation + TTL state in a contract-manager service; it emits intent events to placement controller via a compact API. easier to iterate and safer on restarts.
James: eventual consistency is the tradeoff. we need SLOs for the guaranteed lane unchanged. this only impacts non-guaranteed / best-effort lanes.
Anya: rollout plan: internal test -> small canary (2 tenants) -> opt-in beta -> default-on for non-guaranteed after 6 weeks of telemetry.
Micah: metrics to capture: "lease_rate", "renewal_rate", "decay_score_dist", "churn_flags", "placement_mismatch". set alert when placement_mismatch > 1% over 5m.
Lia: ops runbook note: when churn flags spike, automatically increase renewal_cost and send SE email with sample tenants. also a temporary throttle gate for renewal endpoint.
James: billing: recommend free N renewals per tenant per month, then small metered charge (credits) to discourage aggressive renewals. link to pricing follow-up.
Anya: leadership/HA: contract-manager instances use existing leader-election lock (same as operator) to pick a single reconciler. read-only replicas can serve metrics.
Micah: CLI/API example:
```
POST /v1/leases {
  tenant: "acme",
  target_qps: 12,
  ttl: 120
}
Response: { lease_id: "L-123", expires_at: 1610001200, score: 0.78 }
```
Renewal: same POST -> increments renew_count and recomputes score.
James: server-side bounds: ttl within [30,300], target_qps <= tenant_quota, reject if tenant has active churn penalty.
Lia: telemetry: historical decay_score per tenant to feed offline evals and tune alpha/beta/gamma. we should log renewal timestamps for fraud detection.
Anya: failure modes: 
- contract-manager crash -> placements continue using last cached intents for short grace period (60s).
- stale intents -> placement mismatch metrics show up, trigger rollback to pure reactive placement.
- abuse -> billing + throttle.
Micah: engineering tasks: prototype contract-manager + small API, add score function, wire placement to prefer high-score leases.
James: I'll size billing meter and draft pricing language. Lia: I'll draft alerts + runbook.
